The somatosensory nucleus ventralis posteriolar of the cat thalamus shows two types of rhythmic activity, one of which is probably related to spindle activity in adjacent cortex."
(1) type A rhythmic thalamic activity is coherent with cortical activity, and (2) type B thalamic activity, which has shorter period, is not coherent with cortex.

Rhythmic activity in the somatosensory system is characterized by a relatively stable, long period, type A, pattern, and by a shorter period, type B, pattern which is more variable and which is often accompanied by arrhythmy in adjacent non-primary somatosensory cortex.

VP neurons show rhythmic activity which is correlated with cortical rhythms, but which is also influenced by extrathalamic inputs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the type B activity reflects a relatively unstable, but more intense, oscillatory activity in the thalamus, while type A activity reflects a more stable, but relatively weaker oscillation in the thalamocortical system.
the thalamic activity is not only modulated by the reticular formation but also by cortical and subcortical structures, and that the thalami are not isolated from the rest of the brain.

the thalamus is an essential component of a central oscillator which is responsible for the generation of spindle-like activity, and that the thalamic oscillator is probably controlled by a central pacemaker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a central rhythm generator in the thalalamic nucleus ventroposterior.
there are two different rhythms in VP.
there are multiple rhythms in the somatosensory system and they are not necessarily related to each other.
